Black develops the knight to control the e4 square and keep opening choices flexible.
White fights for control over the d5 square and prepares to develop the knight to c3.
Black prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop to g7 to influence the long diagonal.
White develops the knight to support the e4 push and apply pressure to d5.
Black develops the bishop to the long diagonal, preparing for kingside castling.
White establishes a broad pawn center, controlling d5 and f5.
Black prevents White from advancing e4-e5 and prepares for an eventual e7-e5 strike.
White develops the knight, reinforcing the center and preparing to castle.
Black castles, placing the king in safety and activating the rook.
White enters the Classical Variation, preparing to castle kingside.
Black strikes at the center, contesting White's spatial advantage.

Caro-Kann Defense.explanation: White stakes a claim in the center and prepares to develop the light-squared bishop.
Black prepares to challenge White's e4 pawn with d7-d5 on the next move.
White builds a strong pawn center and controls the c5 and e5 squares.
Black strikes at the e4 pawn immediately, establishing a solid pawn wedge.
White develops a knight to defend e4 and control the center.
Black exchanges pawns, opening lines and preparing to develop the light-squared bishop.
White recaptures, centralizing the knight on e4.
Black develops the bishop with tempo, attacking the centralized knight.
White retreats the knight to safety while harassing the active bishop.
Black retreats the bishop, preserving it on an active diagonal.
